description.text: Rain lashes a tall stone lighthouse standing on a black rocky headland. Huge waves burst white against its base, and a fork of lightning flares behind the tower, briefly throwing the whole structure into silhouette before the dark closes back in. In the extreme wide view, the tower holds its ground while the storm-driven sea churns around the rocks and the sky presses low and heavy. Salt spray streaks the wet stone, and the lantern room glass is dark above the rocks.
Howling wind, rain hammering stone, surf crashing against the rocks, and a distant low thunder roll.
A tall stone lighthouse stands on a black rocky headland as rain lashes the stone and huge waves burst white against its base.
Lightning flares behind the tower and throws the structure into silhouette; the waves surge and break again.
Salt spray streaks the wet stone and the dark closes back around the tower.
The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.

Inside the tower, a soaked lighthouse keeper in a heavy coat and cap climbs a tight spiral staircase. One hand grips the cold iron rail while the other holds a swaying lantern; the flame gutters with each gust that rattles the shuttered windows. His boots strike the worn stone steps in a steady, laboring rhythm as he works upward through the drafty tower. The stairwell is narrow, its curved wall slick with damp, and cold blue storm light leaks through the shutters in thin bars.
The soaked keeper climbs the tight spiral staircase, one hand on the iron rail and the other holding a swaying lantern.
Wind buffets the tower, rain ticks against the shutters, boots sound on stone steps, the lantern handle creaks, and the keeper breathes heavily.
The lantern flame gutters as gusts rattle the shutters; cold blue light leaks through in thin bars.
His boots strike the worn stone steps in a steady, laboring rhythm as he works upward.
The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.

In the lamp room, the keeper sets the lantern down and grips the brass clockwork mechanism with both hands, turning the crank until it catches. He lifts the glass chimney and shields the wick from the draft with his palm. The flame takes with a soft roar, swelling bright and throwing his face into warm relief as the great Fresnel lens begins to turn. Brass fittings gleam in the first warm light, and the lens prisms flash as they start to rotate.
In the lamp room the keeper sets the lantern down and grips the brass clockwork with both hands, turning the crank until it catches.
The clockwork clacks and whirrs, glass and brass rattle in the wind, and the muffled roar of the storm presses in.
He lifts the glass chimney and shields the wick with his palm; the flame takes with a soft roar and swells bright.
The wick hisses and catches with a soft roar as glass and brass rattle in the wind.
Warm light throws his face into relief as the Fresnel lens begins to turn, its prisms flashing.
The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.

From outside the tower, the rotating beam sweeps out in a long white arc across the heaving sea, cutting through the rain. The keeper stands small and silhouetted behind the turning lens in the lamp room, one hand still on the mechanism. The view widens to reveal the illuminated lighthouse holding its light against the storm-covered sea below. Rain streaks the glass, and the white beam throws drifting veils of spray into brief visibility before the dark returns.
The rotating beam sweeps out in a long white arc across the heaving sea, cutting through rain.
A low moan of wind around the tower, rain on glass, surf pounding the rocks, and a faint mechanical hum from the turning lens.
The keeper stands silhouetted behind the turning lens, one hand on the mechanism, as the view widens to the illuminated lighthouse.
The camera pulls out with large amplitude at slow speed.
